children: The share of available Chinese-origin copper stocks in London Metal Exchange warehouses rose to 44% in August from 42% a month earlier, exchange data showed on Thursday, as overall available inventories increased.

Total available copper stocks (0#MCUSTX-LOC) in LME warehouses rose to 111,175 metric tons at the end of August from 101,425 tons at the end of July, as a rush by investors to cover bearish positions pushed prompt copper prices into a sharp backwardation, attracting some inflows.
The volume of Chinese copper available increased by 6,350 tons to 49,400 tons.

Meanwhile, Russian-origin aluminium accounted for 95% of available LME aluminium stocks in August, unchanged from the previous month, despite another small drawdown. Available Russian metal fell by 2,750 tons to 230,050 tons.
Indian material, the only other available origin, was unchanged at 12,450 tons.

Many traders are shunning Russian aluminium even though metal produced before mid-April 2024 remains eligible for trading. Aluminium made in Russia after that date is barred from the LME warehousing system to comply with Western sanctions.
The share of Chinese-origin nickel held steady at 70% of available LME stocks at the end of last month.
